message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights and obligations that apply to most residential lease agreements: | Category | Typical Rights | Typical Responsibilities | |----------|----------------|---------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Must be returned within 30 days after the lease ends (or 45 days if the landlord claims damages).
• Landlord may keep part of the deposit only for unpaid rent, damages beyond normal wear, or other costs specified in the lease. | • Keep the property clean and free of damage.
• Provide a forwarding address for the return of the deposit. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary condition.
• Must repair major problems such as plumbing leaks, heating failures, or structural issues. | • Report needed repairs promptly.
• Keep the unit reasonably clean. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter the unit without proper notice (usually 48 hours) except in emergencies.
• Landlord cannot interfere with your peaceful use of the property. | • Respect the landlord’s right to access for legitimate reasons. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease agreements must be in writing if they last longer than one year.
• Certain clauses (e.g., “no pets” or “no smoking”) are enforceable if clearly stated. | • Sign the lease only after reviewing all terms.
• Follow the lease’s rules regarding pets, guests, and subletting. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease specifies them and they are reasonable. | • Pay rent on time.
• Keep records of payments. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the court‑ordered eviction procedure.
• Tenants have the right to contest an eviction in court. | • Respond to notices promptly.
• Attend court hearings if required. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income. | • Provide truthful information when applying for housing. | | **Health & Safety Codes** | • Landlord must comply with local health and safety codes (e.g., smoke detectors, pest control). | • Report violations to the landlord or local authorities. | | **Utilities & Services** | • Landlord must provide essential utilities (water, heat, electricity) unless otherwise agreed. | • Pay for utilities if the lease requires it. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Read the Lease Carefully** – Make sure you understand every clause before signing. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of the lease, receipts, emails, and photos of the unit’s condition. 3. **Report Problems Promptly** – Notify the landlord in writing about needed repairs. 4. **Know the Notice Requirements** – If you’re moving out, give written notice at least 30 days before the lease ends. 5. **Seek Legal Assistance if Needed** – If you believe your landlord is violating your rights, you can contact a local tenant‑rights organization or consult an attorney. ### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Tenant Rights**: https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumer-protection/tenant-rights - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs**: https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us/ - **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** (search online for nonprofits in your city). These points cover the most common rights and responsibilities for tenants in Texas. If you have a specific situation—such as a dispute over a security deposit, a potential eviction, or a lease clause that seems unfair—you might consider contacting a local attorney or a tenant‑rights nonprofit for tailored guidance.
